projects.name: 42run
projects.description: Do you know the mobile game Temple Run? Time to settle and create it on your own! This OpenGL project aims to create a graphic game using the power of GPUs, manipulating 3D meshes, and implementing classical gameplay features.

projects.name: 42sh
projects.description: This project consists of creating a complete shell. A minimum set of functionalities is asked, from which you will build your own finalized shell, potentially going as far as job control and shell scripting. This project will involve a large variety of standard UNIX (and POSIX) functionalities.

projects.name: Abstract_data
projects.description: The multiple available containers in C++ all have a very different usage. To make sure you understand them all, let's re-implement them!

projects.name: abstract-vm
projects.description: This project gets you back into the flow after the C++ piscine and involves creating a virtual machine capable of executing code in basic pseudo-ASM. You will use a stack for basic arithmetic operations, similar to the dc command.

projects.name: Agent smith
projects.description: This is a project where you build an autonomous AI agent capable of reasoning, generating, executing, and iterating on code to solve programming challenges in a secure, sandboxed environment.

projects.name: avaj-launcher
projects.description: First project of the Java projects arc. Implementation of a simple Java program according to a given class diagram written in UML.

projects.name: B
projects.description: The letter before C

projects.name: Bgp At Doors of Autonomous Systems is Simple
projects.description: The purpose of this project is to deepen your knowledge of NetPractice. You will have to simulate several networks (VXLAN+BGP-EVPN) in GNS3.

projects.name: bomberman
projects.description: Bomberman is a classic video game: as simple in its gameplay as it is fun to play! You will leverage its simplicity here to undertake your first major professional-grade C++ project. Your goal is to recode a version of Bomberman in C++ and OpenGL, with the aim of creating the most polished game possible.

projects.name: boot2root
projects.description: This project introduces computer security through a hands-on challenge: you are given access to a deliberately vulnerable Linux server and must become root by at least two distinct methods. Each path requires reconnaissance, web exploitation, and a chain of privilege escalations across multiple user accounts. You will document every step in a writeup, explain the vulnerability behind each breach, and understand how it could have been prevented.

projects.name: Call Me Maybe
projects.description: This project introduces function calling in Large Language Models by building a system that translates natural language prompts into structured function calls with typed arguments. You'll implement constrained decoding to guarantee valid JSON output, achieving near-perfect reliability with a small 0.5B parameter model, bridging the gap between human language and computer-executable operations.

projects.name: camagru
projects.description: This project is a warm-up for web development. You will need to create a small, Instagram-like website that allows users to create and share photomontages. From scratch, you will implement the basic functionalities commonly used by any website with a user base.

projects.name: cc1
projects.description: This project is about creating a C compiler

projects.name: churn
projects.description: This project is an introduction to artificial neural nets: fully-connected neural nets, hidden layers, activation functions, back-propagation, dropout

projects.name: cinema
projects.description: Let's expand your knowledge of Java web development using the Spring stack and master Hibernate framework

projects.name: City Life
projects.description: This project is an introduction to geospatial analytics: GeoPandas, clustering, making maps

projects.name: cloud-1
projects.description: This project is an introduction to cloud servers.

projects.name: computorv1
projects.description: The goal of this project is to get acquainted with handling elementary math tools that may be helpful for other 42 projects. You will not “do math for doing math”, but to develop a progressive and relaxed approach to projects where these tools are needed. You can choose the language of your choice for this subject.

projects.name: computorv2
projects.description: Now that you have programmed your equation solver, it’s time to go further. Computor V2 lets you create your own calculator from the command line, which will integrate your Computor V1 as well as functions for matrix calculus, function solving, calculations with complex numbers, and more.

projects.name: corewar
projects.description: This project involves creating a virtual arena, and having simplistic-language programs fight each other. You will thus get acquainted with VM conception (with instructions it recognizes, registers, etc) and compilation problems of an assembly language in bytecode. In bonus, the pleasure to have your champions fight in the arena.

projects.name: Cybersecurity
projects.description: Piscines are an important time in your cursus, during which you will have the occasion to learn a new language, or even a new paradigm!

projects.name: darkly
projects.description: Introductory project to computer security in the specific field of the web, this project has you audit a deliberately vulnerable web platform. You will exploit real-world vulnerabilities to escalate your access from an anonymous visitor all the way up to administrator, capture the flags hidden along the way, and understand how each breach could have been prevented, both from a programming and a design perspective.

projects.name: Datomic
projects.description: Datomic is a databases project. On a single self-contained VM you climb twenty levels across six engines (SQLite, PostgreSQL, Redis, ClickHouse, Neo4j and DuckDB), building up SQL and then moving on to columnar, key-value and graph stores. The point is not the syntax of six databases but knowing which tool fits which problem, and federating them instead of duplicating data. Every level draws from a bank of validated variants and your data is renamed for your login, so nobody hands you a solved copy. You discover the SQL yourself in a browser playground and prove it in a live review exam, with nothing to hand in.

projects.name: death
projects.description: Last virus project. Create with your Famine, Pestilence and War a real metamorphic code.

projects.name: doom-nukem
projects.description: Doom Nukem pushes the possibilities of Raycasting much further while bringing a dimension of Game design, so you are going to have to make a mix of Doom and Duke Nukem 3D. It's up to you to find the one that suits you and that will allow you to add the requested features as well as those you want to see there.

projects.name: dr-quine
projects.description: This small algo project will get you acquainted with auto-replication problems and confront the Kleene recursion theorem.

projects.name: drivers-and-interrupts
projects.description: Learn how to connect a driver to your kernel. We will use a keyboard driver for this project.

projects.name: dslr
projects.description: Discover Data Science through this project by recreating the Hogwarts Sorting Hat using logistic regression!

projects.name: Ecomesh
projects.description: One deployment, one year, zero reset. A mesh of battery-powered sensors is dropped in a nature reserve with no way back in: no recharge, no replacement, no repair. Your job is not to build the network, it is to keep it alive and honest. You build, in code, a real carbon cost model of the system using the Software Carbon Intensity standard, accounting for both the energy the nodes spend and the carbon embodied in the hardware itself, including what is stranded for good when a node runs out of battery or wears out early. Then you design an adaptive policy that spreads component wear and places computation, so no single node burns out and drags a whole branch of the mesh down with it. Everything runs on real Contiki-NG firmware inside a headless Cooja / MSPSim emulation, on a procedurally generated scenario you have never seen and cannot memorize. By the end, you can explain every decision in terms of the Green Software Engineering principles it serves.

projects.name: expert-system
projects.description: This project involves creating, in the language of your choice, an expert system in proposal calculation. In other words, a program that can reason on a set of rules and initial facts to deduce other facts.

projects.name: famine
projects.description: Welcome to the wonderful world of viruses, trojans and other <Insert random antiVirus software>… Your goal here is to put your skills on handling binary files and make your first virus. WARNING: this project is solely for educational purposes!

projects.name: filesystem
projects.description: Create your own filesystem, for your linux kernel.

projects.name: fix-me
projects.description: Final project of the Java Programming arc. You will write a program that simulates stock exchanges and handles trading algorithms, including networking and socket implementations.

projects.name: freddie-mercury
projects.description: VR escape game

projects.name: Fried eggs
projects.description: This project is an introduction to Deep Learning and computer vision (CNN, instance segmentation, object detection, data labeling)

projects.name: ft_ality
projects.description: This project will get you acquainted with problems linked to automatic syntax analysis (“parsin”) by studying finite automation in a combat game.

projects.name: ft_hangouts
projects.description: The goal of this project is to introduce you to mobile application development. You will build a contact management app for Android, allowing users to create, manage, and interact with their contacts. Throughout the project, you will learn how a mobile app works, how the Android system manages application lifecycles, and how to use the Android SDK effectively.

projects.name: ft_kalman
projects.description: Aboard a generic vehicle with flawed sensors, you will need to create a kalman filter in order to track his position coordinates. This project is a good introduction to signal filtering, matrix operations, gaussian noise and correlation.

projects.name: ft_kleene
projects.description: Delve deep into the mathematics of computer science by learning how programming languages and compilers are built: through language theory and automata theory !

projects.name: ft_lex
projects.description: A project about lexical analysis and finite automata. In this project you will implement a powerful regex engine

projects.name: ft_lgtm
projects.description: Build a web application that runs untrusted code securely with WASM/WASI, uploads it to IPFS, and monitors everything with a complete LGTM observability stack on Kubernetes.

projects.name: ft_linear_regression
projects.description: This project will be your first steps into AI and Machine Learning. You're going to start with a simple, basic machine learning algorithm. You will have to create a program that predicts the price of a car by using a linear function train with a gradient descent algorithm.

projects.name: ft_linux
projects.description: The first project of the Kernel branch! This is a simple LFS so that you can build your own distribution which will be used in the next projects

projects.name: ft_ls
projects.description: For knowing the filesystem inside out, and how files and directories are sorted, you will code by yourself one of the most used command: ls.

projects.name: ft_microservices
projects.description: Now you will master the skills of creating microservice applications using Spring framework

projects.name: ft_minecraft
projects.description: ft_minecraft is the continuation of ft_vox, with a more advanced approach to procedural generation, rendering techniques and networking.

projects.name: ft_newton
projects.description: Basic physics engine - motion - gravity - collisions.

projects.name: ft_nmap
projects.description: Re-coding the nmap command will be the opportunity to deepen your knowledge of TCP/IP networks and thus understand advanced use of threads in real life.

projects.name: ft_ping
projects.description: Re-coding the ping command will allow you to become acquainted with raw IP communication between two machines on a network.

projects.name: ft_resume
projects.description: Build your communication and self-reflection skills by working closely with a peer. Through mutual interviews, you’ll learn to recognize and express both your strengths and theirs—helping you craft genuine, effective resumes.

projects.name: ft_script
projects.description: By re-coding the script command you will have the opportunity to understand interactions between user input and tty, notably line discipline as well as pseudo-terminals. Once the project finished, you will know why a Ctrl-C in your shell interrupts the ongoing program!

projects.name: ft_select
projects.description: The goal of this project is to get you started on terminal manipulation with termcaps. Here you will learn how to create a user interface for a program launched on the terminal.

projects.name: ft_shield
projects.description: Use your skills to create a daemon to create your first basic trojan.

projects.name: ft_ssl_des
projects.description: You will reimplement part of the OpenSSL program, specifically BASE64, DES-ECB, and DES-CBC.

projects.name: ft_ssl_md5
projects.description: You will recode part of the OpenSSL program, specifically the MD5 Hashing Algorithm.

projects.name: ft_ssl_rsa
projects.description: You will code your own random prime number generator and use it to make private RSA keys.

projects.name: ft_traceroute
projects.description: Re-coding the traceroute command will be the opportunity to deepen your knowledge of TCP/IP networks by following the paths of an IP packet from one machine to another.

projects.name: ft_turing
projects.description: ft_turing will help you discover the turing model using imperative programming through an implementation of this model with OCaml

projects.name: ft_vox
projects.description: ft_vox is a project that introduces voxel engines, inspired by Minecraft, where you must create a randomly generated world.

projects.name: ft_yacc
projects.description: A project about syntactic analysis and stack automata

projects.name: Ftl_quantum
projects.description: This project is an introduction to quantum programming. It will challenge you to create different quantum programs, and run them on a real quantum computer.

projects.name: fwa
projects.description: in this project you will develop your First Web Application using standard Java technologies

projects.name: gomoku
projects.description: This project involves creating, in the language of your choice, a Gomoku game integrating an AI player capable of beating a human player the fastest way possible. To do this, you will implement a min-max algorithm but also do research, trial and error to find the most adapted heuristics. This will not be as easy as checkers.

projects.name: guimp
projects.description: The goal of this project is to create a graphic interface library. You will have to prove it works correctly with a small 2D image software. This library must as complete and modular as possible, the goal being to re-use it in future projects, whether for projects in the graphic branch or other projects of you training.

projects.name: h42n42
projects.description: An introductory project to the OCSIGEN framework for creating rich web applications in OCaml. The goal is to design a simulator where creatures try to escape a dangerous virus.

projects.name: humangl
projects.description: This intermediate OpenGL project is an introduction to hierarchical modeling. You will learn to use matrices in order to link various parts of a humanoid model, and animate them.

projects.name: hypertube
projects.description: Hypertube introduces you to a powerful category of tools: MVC frameworks. You will learn how to work with an MVC framework—using the programming language of your choice—to build a video streaming website with content downloaded via the BitTorrent protocol.

projects.name: in-the-shadows
projects.description: This project wants you to develop a complete game using a bit of algo and a lot of creativity.

projects.name: Inception of context
projects.description: Every senior team now ships with an AI coding assistant. Most engineers use one; almost nobody has built one. In this project you build your own, end to end on your laptop: a local model, a vector index over your code, a retriever that answers grounded questions, and a patch loop that applies, validates, and rolls back when things break. No cloud, no API key, no token bill. By the end, you will know how Copilot and Cursor actually work, because you will have built one.

projects.name: Inception of wisdom
projects.description: Autonomous self-healing on your laptop. The agent watches a real service, notices when it crashes, retrieves the relevant code and config from its own index, asks a local language model what to change, applies the patch, commits it, restarts the service, and rolls everything back when the fix does not take. This project ties together what Inception-of-Things taught about GitOps-driven deployment and what Inception-of-Context taught about retrieval-augmented patching, into a closed observe / think / act / verify loop that never leaves the project broken. By the end, you will have an agent that catches a bug you planted, finds it without your help, fixes it, and proves it stayed fixed.

projects.name: Inception-of-Things
projects.description: This project aims to introduce you to Kubernetes from a developer's perspective. You will have to set up small clusters and discover the mechanics of continuous integration. At the end of this project, you will be able to set up a working cluster in Docker and have a usable continuous integration pipeline for your applications.

projects.name: kfs-6

projects.name: kfs-7

projects.name: kfs-8

projects.name: malloc

projects.description: This second project introduces a more advanced tool for building web applications: the micro-framework. You are invited to create a dating site in the programming language of your choice. User interaction is at the heart of this project!

projects.name: matrix
projects.description: You've probably encountered vectors and vector spaces before. Now it's time to formalize them through Linear Algebra and to learn how matrices and linear transformations work.

projects.description: In a group, create a complete mobile app for collaborative playlists using a relevant SDK and API. The tasks include mobile development, back-end development, and the creation of a REST API.

projects.name: mySpotify
projects.description: This project is an introduction to algorithms used for recommendations: non-personalized, content-based, collaborative filtering.

projects.name: n-puzzle

Rainfall taught you the stack; Override drops you into modern, fully mitigated 64-bit binaries on glibc 2.39, all protections on by default. Stripped binaries, no shortcuts, the heap and the network in play. This is serious binary exploitation. Come prepared.

projects.name: rainfall
projects.description: Rainfall picks up where Snow Crash left off and goes deeper. On a deliberately vulnerable VM, you climb from one account to the next by exploiting a series of SUID ELF binaries: reading their code, mapping how they lay out memory, and turning their flaws into control of execution. Each level tightens the protections (NX, stack canaries and ASLR), so your techniques must grow with them. Full RELRO and PIE await in the bonus part. Will you reach the last level?

You will become familiar with technical documentation, better apprehend hardware emulation and understand the inner workings of a real piece of hardware as well as ROM cartridges.

projects.name: rt
projects.description: RT pushes the limits of what Ray Tracing can do: mirror effect, transparency, object cutting, texture application... . Use the preceding project to create an infrastructure capable of supporting all these ramifications and obtain sublime computer-generated images.

projects.name: rubik

projects.name: scop
projects.description: Your introduction to 3D rendering on the GPU using OpenGL, Vulkan, or Metal. Through this small graphical project, you'll explore the core concepts of modern 3D graphics.

projects.name: shaderpixel
projects.description: Now that you are familiar with 3D objects and basic rendering techniques, we can get serious now and really work in the space of the graphic card. It’s up to you to design and create the weirdest objects thanks to shaders programming.

projects.name: snow-crash
projects.description: Eleven independent security challenges on a deliberately vulnerable Linux VM. Each level requires a distinct technique: binary analysis, process and filesystem inspection, code injection through configuration files and templates, protocol reverse engineering, jail escapes, and side-channel attacks. You will learn to read and exploit systems you did not write, using the tools and mindset of a security researcher.

projects.name: strace
projects.description: First step in a serie of projects in C language leading to creation of a mini-GDB, this project will ask you to recode strace, a tool allowing you to list syscalls done by a running program

projects.name: Supercharge

projects.name: swifty-companion
projects.description: This project is an introduction to mobile programming. The goal is to create, an application which will allow you to get infos about 42students, using the API.

projects.name: swifty-proteins
projects.description: Build a professional mobile application for visualizing protein ligands in 3D. You'll fetch molecular data from the RCSB Protein Data Bank, parse Chemical Information Files (.cif format), and render complex molecular structures using native 3D frameworks (SceneKit on iOS or equivalent on Android). The app features secure biometric authentication, interactive 3D models with CPK coloring and ball-and-stick representation, gesture-based controls for rotation and zoom, and social sharing capabilities. This project combines bioinformatics, mobile security, network programming, and advanced 3D graphics rendering.

projects.description: This project was designed by the Daher company and has you develop a graphic interface under Unity for optimizing industrial processes.

projects.name: zappy
projects.description: You will now create a multi-player game in a TCP/IP network. The game will consist of a server managing the game field, a graphic client which displays the state of the board, and IA clients that connect to the server to pilot a player on the filed. This is a real complete project that will let you express your creativity on top of your technical knowledge.
